key_highlights: ASX flat overall; miners and tech lead gains while oil stocks lag; Myer jumps on consumer optimism
Australian flash PMI sags, signalling softening domestic activity amid RBA rate-hike pressure on household spending
Global diesel shortage (Iran/Ukraine) to persist into 2027; Saudi oil shock spikes Australian fuel prices
Gold and rare-earths sector active: Critical Resources surges on Suriname grab; Critica WA Jupiter rare-earths offtake; Greenland rare-earths pact lifts Critical Metals 35%
Coalition threatens to dismantle climate laws and offshore wind; Labor energy-cost credibility questioned
Property market cooling: rising listings, falling demand pushing prices lower; Chinese property recovery uncertain
Jetstar industrial action escalates with fee waivers; Qantas confirms Sydney-New York non-stop schedule
Federal and state governments face mounting debt pressures; migration and demographic concerns intensify

sectors.trend: Miners rise on ASX; gold exploration names (Critical Resources, Aurum, Platina, Dalaroo, Advance, Broken Hill) active on project milestones; rare-earths (Critica, Critical Metals) boosted by Greenland pact and offtake deals
sectors.implications: Gold and rare-earths sub-sectors offer relative strength; iron ore/coal exposure remains vulnerable to China rebalancing and property uncertainty

sectors.trend: Oil stocks struggle on ASX despite Saudi shock; diesel shortage to last into 2027; Coalition-Labor energy policy clash; data-centre demand threatens net-zero targets
sectors.implications: Fuel-cost inflation pressures consumer and transport names; policy uncertainty around offshore wind and climate legislation creates regulatory risk for energy transition plays

sectors.trend: Tech stocks lead ASX higher following Wall Street surge; AI processing and semiconductor themes active globally
sectors.implications: ASX tech exposure (limited) benefits from global risk-on; data-centre buildout supports power and infrastructure demand

sectors.trend: Myer jumps; RBA rate hikes squeeze household spending; Jetstar industrial action; El Nino threatens agricultural supply chains
sectors.implications: Consumer discretionary under pressure from higher fuel costs and tighter credit; industrial action at Jetstar (JLH.AX) adds operational risk

sectors.trend: RBA rate-hike cycle compresses household budgets; ACCC blocks RAC WA insurance sale; government debt pressures mount
sectors.implications: Bank NIMs supported by higher rates but credit-quality risk rises; insurance consolidation stalled; sovereign debt trajectory a medium-term concern

sectors.trend: Syngenis gains precision-medicine firepower; uranium stocks rally on nuclear renaissance theme
sectors.implications: ASX-listed biotech and med-tech names benefit from global innovation cycle; uranium exposure (NEXT.AX, NEX.AX) supported by nuclear demand

sectors.trend: Rising listings and falling demand push property prices lower; Chinese property recovery uncertain
sectors.implications: Australian REITs (GPG.AX, ICPS.AX) face headwinds from weaker demand; China exposure via mining REITs remains a wildcard

key_themes: RBA tightening cycle vs softening PMI – household spending under pressure
Global diesel/fuel supply shock (Iran, Ukraine) extending into 2027
Gold and rare-earths exploration momentum across WA and Africa
Energy policy gridlock: Coalition anti-climate stance vs Labor credibility gap
Property market cooling domestically; China recovery still unconfirmed
Industrial action in aviation (Jetstar, Virgin) disrupting consumer travel
Government debt trajectory and migration/demographic policy uncertainty

risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge transport and consumer exposure; favour energy producers with integrated fuel supply

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate-hike cycle squeezing household spending and credit quality
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce consumer-discretionary weight; favour dividend-paying financials with strong capital buffers

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Energy policy uncertainty (offshore wind, climate legislation)
risk_assessment.mitigation: Avoid policy-dependent renewable names until political clarity; favour established energy majors

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Property market downturn and Chinese property uncertainty
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight REITs; monitor Chinese property data for mining-demand signals

risk_assessment.risk_factor: El Nino impact on agricultural supply and food inflation
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor BHP.AX iron ore and CSL.AX as relative hedges; reduce ag-exposed consumer staples

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Government debt cliff and fiscal sustainability
risk_assessment.mitigation: Watch 10-year GBA yield; favour inflation-linked or short-duration bonds

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and rare-earths exploration names on project catalysts
opportunities.rationale: Multiple ASX-listed juniors (Critical Resources, Aurum, Platina, Dalaroo, Advance) hitting milestones; Greenland rare-earths pact and Critica offtake signal sector tailwind

opportunities.recommendation: Add uranium exposure on nuclear renaissance theme
opportunities.rationale: Uranium stocks rallying; NXE initiated at Overweight; data-centre power demand supports long-term nuclear buildout

opportunities.recommendation: Selective tech allocation on global risk-on
opportunities.rationale: Tech leads ASX after Wall Street surge; AI processing and semiconductor themes active

defensive_moves.rationale: RBA hikes, diesel shock, and Jetstar/Virgin industrial action compress margins and consumer spending
Rising listings, falling demand, and Chinese property uncertainty pressure valuations

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge fuel-cost inflation via energy majors
defensive_moves.rationale: Diesel shortage into 2027 supports upstream earnings; WES and BHP offer dividend protection

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound (5,800–6,100 ^AXJO) with sector rotation: miners and tech outperform, oil and consumer lag. PMI softness and RBA pressure cap upside; diesel shock adds volatility. Myer and tech provide pockets of strength.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA pauses and PMI stabilises. Gold/rare-earths and uranium offer structural tailwinds. Property and consumer remain vulnerable. China recovery confirmation would lift iron ore and coal names. Fiscal debt trajectory is the key macro overhang.
key_catalysts: RBA cash rate decision and CPI print
El Nino progression and ag output
watch_list: Iron ore, gold, LNG spot prices
RBA cash rate and forward guidance
